title: Function routing & argument sanitization evaluation suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a reusable, automated evaluation harness that measures two orthogonal dimensions for function/tool-style calls after model or config changes: 1) routing/selection accuracy (did the model choose the correct function/tool from the available set), and 2) argument sanitization & validity (are the chosen arguments syntactically and semantically valid for the selected function). This harness should run on PRs that touch routing/config code and nightly against production model variants.

Motivation: recent regressions around function selection after kernel and quantization changes have produced silent correctness failures. We need an observable way to detect selection drift and argument-level regressions tied to model, tokenization, or runtime flags so rollbacks or mitigations can be automated.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: selection accuracy metric, arg validation checks (types, required fields, schema conformance), regression alerting on threshold violations, CI integration, nightly runs, dashboard events.
- Out-of-scope: building a universal argument fuzzer for all third-party tools (we'll start with canonical in-house tool set), full automated rollback (we will provide alert + recommended mitigation).

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness can run end-to-end against a model variant and a given routing/config snapshot and output per-case verdicts (correct-selection|wrong-selection|partial-match|no-call).
- Argument validation returns PASS/FAIL with error classifications (missing-field, type-mismatch, out-of-range, unsafe-value).
- Selection accuracy and arg PASS-rate computed per model/config and persisted to time-series store nightly.
- CI check: any PR that changes routing, routing-config, or function schemas triggers the harness; failing PRs must be marked with a red check and include failure summary.
- Alerts: daily and immediate alerts when running baseline model -> new-variant delta exceeds 2% absolute drop in selection accuracy or when arg PASS-rate drops >3%. Alerts posted to #evals-regressions with links to failing examples and suggested mitigations.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Golden labels: we will combine a curated human-labeled corpus (template and edge prompts) with telemetry-derived canonical cases from production logs. Human labels for selection may disagree; we'll store majority label and uncertainty score.
- Coverage vs cost: running full candidate set (all functions) for every prompt is expensive. Use stratified sampling for nightly runs (heavy-tail distribution), full sweep on PRs touching routing.
- Argument validation: implement schema-driven checks using existing tool schemas in the repo. For semantic checks (e.g., URL reachability, domain whitelists) we will implement lightweight syntactic validation first and add semantic probes later as opt-in.
- Failure modes: model may select a compatible but lower-preference tool; we classify compatible-but-suboptimal as partial-match (lower severity) to reduce noisy alerts.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Harness runner and result proto: define flat CSV/JSONL result rows with fields (prompt_id, model_variant, config_hash, selected_tool, selection_label, args_json_string, arg_result_code, runtime_metadata, example_reference_url).
2) Integrate with existing evals infra and time-series (Wavefront/Prometheus) for metrics export.
3) Add CI hook: PR linter identifies touched files (routing/, function-schemas/) and enqueues PR-run.
4) Nightly pipeline: sample dataset, run against baseline and candidate variants, compute deltas, persist, and emit alerts.
5) Dashboard: small Grafana panel with selection_accuracy, arg_pass_rate, and top failing examples linking to stored JSONL.

Metrics to monitor:
- selection_accuracy (per model, per config)
- arg_pass_rate (per tool)
- false_positive_rate of argument validator (tracked via human triage tags)
- time-to-detect (from model/config change to alert)

Test plan:
- Unit tests for schema validation and result serialization.
- PR-level smoke runs on a minimal seed set (10-50 cases) to validate behavior quickly.
- Nightly run on full sample (5000–20k examples depending on sampling) with historical baseline comparison.
- Manual review board for initial 2 weeks after rollout to tune thresholds.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 1 (week 1): run harness internally against canary models; keep alerts muted but persist results.
- Phase 2 (week 2): enable CI gating for routing/config PRs with opt-out tag.
- Phase 3 (week 3–4): enable nightly alerts to #evals-regressions and add dashboard panels to runtime-1.24 release notes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Noisy alerts: start with conservative thresholds and majority-labeled golden set. Tune after 2-week observation window.
- Cost of run: use stratified sampling and incremental runs on PRs. Pre-warm workers for repeated PR runs.
- Schema drift: add a compatibility check that skips obsolete examples when schemas evolve and flags manual triage.

Deliverables & sub-tasks:
- ENG-17646: eval runner library and result format (dependency)
- ENG-17647: CI integration + PR gating
- ENG-17648: Nightly pipeline and alerting
- ENG-17649: Dashboard panels and example storage
- ENG-17650: Golden corpus curation + labeling work
